title: A Modern Way to Eat
author: Anna Jones
blurb: A Modern Way to Eat is a vegetarian cookbook by Anna Jones, a London food writer and former Jamie Oliver team member. It collects more than 150 recipes built around vegetables, grains, and pulses, organized by meal and by the way people cook day to day.

title: Batch
author: Joel MacCharles; Dana Harrison
blurb: Batch is a preserving cookbook by Joel MacCharles and Dana Harrison, the Canadian couple behind the Well Preserved blog. It collects small-batch recipes for jams, pickles, ferments, and sauces, organized around cooking and canning in modest quantities at home.

title: Bread Recipes
author: Better Homes & Gardens
blurb: A Better Homes & Gardens collection of bread recipes for home bakers. It covers yeast loaves, quick breads, rolls, and flatbreads, with step by step guidance written for cooks at a range of skill levels.

title: Canal House Cooks Every Day
author: Melissa Hamilton; Christopher Hirsheimer
blurb: Canal House Cooks Every Day is a seasonal cookbook from Melissa Hamilton and Christopher Hirsheimer, the pair behind the Canal House series. It gathers simple recipes, photographs, and notes from their studio kitchen in Lambertville, New Jersey, arranged by month of the year.

title: Classic French Recipes
author: Ginette Mathiot
blurb: Classic French Recipes is a translated edition of Ginette Mathiot's long-running French home-cooking collection. It gathers traditional dishes from soups and sauces to meat, fish, vegetables, and desserts, with short, practical instructions for everyday cooks.

title: Cook This Book
author: Molly Baz
blurb: Molly Baz's 2021 cookbook is built around approachable recipes and a conversational teaching style. Baz, a former Bon Appétit editor, organizes the book around techniques and flavor ideas that help home cooks improvise with confidence in their own kitchens.

title: Dinner
author: Melissa Clark
blurb: Dinner: Changing the Game is a cookbook by New York Times food writer Melissa Clark. It offers weeknight recipes for home cooks, with a focus on quick preparation, flexible ingredients, and dishes that range from simple suppers to meals for guests.

title: Dinner in an Instant
author: Melissa Clark
blurb: Dinner in an Instant is a pressure cooker cookbook by Melissa Clark, a New York Times food writer. It adapts weeknight dishes, soups, braises, grains, and desserts for the electric multicooker, with recipes built around speed and common ingredients.

title: Eaten, No. 5, Spring/Summer 2019
blurb: Eaten is an independent magazine about the history and culture of food, published in issue form. Number five, from Spring and Summer 2019, collects essays and illustrated features that trace how particular dishes, ingredients, and eating habits developed over time.

title: From the Oven to the Table
author: Diana Henry
blurb: From the Oven to the Table is a cookbook by the British food writer Diana Henry. It presents simple dishes cooked in a single roasting pan, tray, or casserole, with chapters on roasts, bakes, and puddings and an emphasis on minimal washing up.

title: Genius Recipes
author: Kristen Miglore
blurb: Genius Recipes is a collection by Kristen Miglore, drawn from her Food52 column of the same name. Each recipe comes from a notable cook or chef and includes a technique or shortcut that changes how a familiar dish is made.

title: Gordon Ramsay: Kitchen Heaven
author: Gordon Ramsay
blurb: Gordon Ramsay: Kitchen Heaven is a cookbook by the Scottish chef, with recipes drawn from his restaurant career and his home cooking. It covers starters, mains, and desserts, and pairs each recipe with Ramsay's tips on technique and ingredients.

title: Healing Mushrooms
author: Tero Isokauppila
blurb: Healing Mushrooms is a guide by Tero Isokauppila, a Finnish founder of a functional mushroom company. It covers varieties such as reishi, chaga, and cordyceps, summarizes their traditional and modern uses, and includes recipes for adding them to drinks and meals.

title: Heat
author: Bill Buford
blurb: Heat is a memoir by New Yorker writer Bill Buford about leaving his editing job to work in the kitchen of Mario Batali's Babbo restaurant in New York. It follows his apprenticeships in Italy, including studies in pasta making and butchery with Italian masters.

title: Home Made
author: Yvette van Boven
blurb: Home Made is a cookbook by Dutch food writer and illustrator Yvette van Boven. Her recipes are arranged around everyday cooking at home, and the book mixes her own drawings and photographs with dishes for baking, preserving, and family meals.

title: Homebrewed Vinegar
author: Kirsten K. Shockey
blurb: Homebrewed Vinegar is a how-to guide by fermentation author Kirsten K. Shockey. It explains how to make vinegar from fruit, grains, vegetables, and other ingredients at home, and it includes recipes for using the finished vinegars in cooking and drinks.

title: Indian(-ish)
author: Priya Krishna
blurb: Indian(-ish) is a cookbook by Priya Krishna built around the home cooking of her mother, Ritu, in Dallas, Texas. The recipes blend Indian flavors with American ingredients and family improvisation, and the book includes stories from the Krishna household.

title: Lemons
author: Gennaro Contaldo
blurb: The book is a cookbook devoted to lemons, from Gennaro Contaldo, the Italian chef from the Amalfi Coast who mentored Jamie Oliver. Published in English as Gennaro's Limoni, it gathers recipes for small plates, pasta, desserts, drinks, and preserves.

title: Lucky Peach: 101 Easy Asian Recipes
author: Peter Meehan; the editors of Lucky Peach
blurb: Lucky Peach: 101 Easy Asian Recipes collects quick dishes from the food magazine Lucky Peach, written with David Chang's Momofuku circle. Peter Meehan and the editors present recipes drawing on Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and Southeast Asian cooking, aimed at cooks working with a modest pantry.

title: My Bombay Kitchen
author: Niloufer Ichaporia King
blurb: My Bombay Kitchen presents the traditional home cooking of the Parsi community of Bombay, written by Niloufer Ichaporia King, an anthropologist and cook who divides her time between India and California. It mixes recipes, family history, and notes on Parsi customs, ingredients, and festivals.

title: Simple
author: Yotam Ottolenghi
blurb: Simple is a cookbook by Yotam Ottolenghi, the London chef and food writer. Each recipe is organized by an acronym of qualities such as short on time, ten ingredients or fewer, or make ahead, so cooks can choose dishes by effort.

title: Soups, Salads, Sandwiches
author: Matty Matheson
blurb: Soups, Salads, Sandwiches is a cookbook by Matty Matheson, a Canadian chef and television personality. It presents recipes for the three title categories in his hearty, informal style, ranging from classic comfort dishes to restaurant-influenced creations.

title: Speaking in Cod Tongues
author: Lenore Newman
blurb: Speaking in Cod Tongues is a Canadian culinary travelogue by Lenore Newman, a geographer who studies food. She crosses Canada from coast to coast to examine the country's regional dishes and food traditions, and asks what a national cuisine might include.

title: The Bread Baker's Apprentice
author: Peter Reinhart
blurb: Peter Reinhart's The Bread Baker's Apprentice is a guide to making artisan bread at home. It follows the stages of bread making, from mixing and fermentation to shaping and baking, and presents formulas for loaves such as ciabatta, pain au levain, and bagels.

title: The Cooking of the Eastern Mediterranean
author: Paula Wolfert
blurb: The Cooking of the Eastern Mediterranean is a cookbook by Paula Wolfert, the American writer known for her work on Mediterranean food. It gathers 215 recipes from countries such as Greece, Turkey, Lebanon, and Syria, with notes on ingredients, techniques, and regional traditions.

title: The Hot Bread Kitchen Cookbook
author: Jessamyn Waldman Rodriguez
blurb: The Hot Bread Kitchen Cookbook collects recipes from the New York bakery of the same name, founded by Jessamyn Waldman Rodriguez. The bakery trains women from immigrant communities as bakers, and the book covers breads from many cultures along with the stories behind them.

title: The New Sotheby's Wine Encyclopedia
author: Tom Stevenson
blurb: The New Sotheby's Wine Encyclopedia is a reference work by wine writer Tom Stevenson. It surveys the world's wine regions, grape varieties, producers, and winemaking methods, with maps and photographs, and has been revised through several editions.

title: The New York Times Cooking: No-Recipe Recipes
author: Sam Sifton
blurb: The New York Times Cooking: No-Recipe Recipes is a cookbook by Sam Sifton, the founding editor of New York Times Cooking. It describes dishes through loose guidelines instead of exact measurements, encouraging home cooks to improvise with what they have on hand.

title: The Wurst! The Very Best of German Food
author: Otto Wolff
blurb: The Wurst! is a short illustrated guide to German food by Melbourne-based writer and cook Otto Wolff. It offers recipes for sausages, schnitzel, pretzels, potato salads, cakes, and other German staples, alongside notes on regional specialties.

author: Will Ferguson
blurb: 419 is a 2012 novel by Canadian author Will Ferguson. It follows a Canadian woman who investigates her father's death after he falls victim to an advance fee email scam, and the story moves between Ontario and Nigeria.

title: A Recipe for Bees
author: Gail Anderson-Dargatz
blurb: A Recipe for Bees is a novel by the Canadian author Gail Anderson-Dargatz. It follows Augusta Olsen, a woman in her seventies who reflects on her long marriage and her family history while keeping bees on a farm in British Columbia.

title: A Sentimental Journey Through France and Italy
author: Laurence Sterne
blurb: A Sentimental Journey Through France and Italy is an unfinished comic travel novel by Laurence Sterne, published in 1768. Its narrator, the clergyman Yorick, records small encounters and feelings on his trip, in a book written after Sterne's Tristram Shandy.

title: A Song of Stone
author: Iain Banks
blurb: A Song of Stone is a 1997 novel by Iain Banks, published without the M in his byline. Set in a nameless European country torn by civil war, it follows an aristocratic couple in their castle as soldiers take control of their lives.

title: Accordion Crimes
author: E. Annie Proulx
blurb: Accordion Crimes is a 1996 novel by E. Annie Proulx. It follows a single green accordion as it passes between owners across a century of American life, tracing immigrant communities from Sicilians and Germans to Mexicans and Cajuns.

title: Am Hang
author: Markus Werner
blurb: Am Hang is a German-language novel by the Swiss writer Markus Werner, published in 1985. Two men meet at a hotel terrace in the mountains and talk about love, failure, and their lives, and the conversation shapes the course of the novel.

title: Brick Lane
author: Monica Ali
blurb: Brick Lane is the 2003 debut novel by Monica Ali. It follows Nazneen, a Bangladeshi woman who moves to London for an arranged marriage and builds a life in the East End community around Brick Lane.

title: Catch-22
author: Joseph Heller
blurb: Catch-22 is Joseph Heller's 1961 satirical novel set among a US Army Air Forces bomber squadron in Italy during the Second World War. Captain John Yossarian tries to survive his required missions while military bureaucracy keeps raising the number, and the paradox of the title governs his options.

title: Dead Air
author: Iain Banks
blurb: Dead Air is a novel by Iain Banks, published in 2002 and set in London after the attacks of September 2001. Its narrator is a loud, opinionated radio shock jock whose life becomes tangled in a series of personal and criminal troubles.

title: Dead Souls
author: Nikolai Gogol
blurb: Dead Souls is an 1842 Russian novel by Nikolai Gogol. Its protagonist, Chichikov, travels the provinces buying the names of dead serfs who still count on tax rolls, and meets a gallery of landowners along the way.

title: Der Coup von Berdac
author: Michael Roes
blurb: A German-language book by Michael Roes, a writer and filmmaker whose novels and essays often grow out of long stays abroad.

title: Ein Sommer in Niendorf
author: Heinz Strunk
blurb: Ein Sommer in Niendorf is a 2022 German-language comic novel by Heinz Strunk. A 51-year-old Hamburg business lawyer rents a seaside apartment on the Baltic coast to write his family's history, and the summer brings encounters with other holidaymakers and locals.

title: First Person Singular
author: Haruki Murakami
blurb: First Person Singular is a 2020 collection of eight short stories by Haruki Murakami. Narrators look back on episodes from their lives, and the settings range from Tokyo to the baseball field to a talking monkey's confession.

title: Habitus
author: James Flint
blurb: Habitus is a 2004 novel by the British writer James Flint. Its story of a man pursuing a lost love moves through cultures and cities, with themes of technology, nomadic living, and the shifting relationship between people and the places they inhabit.

title: Heimatmuseum
author: Siegfried Lenz
blurb: Heimatmuseum is a 1978 German novel by Siegfried Lenz, set in Masuria in what was then East Prussia. Its narrator tells the history of his family and region, and the fate of his local museum, against the backdrop of the Nazi era and its aftermath.

title: Herr Lehmann
author: Sven Regener
blurb: Herr Lehmann is a 2001 novel by Sven Regener, the singer of the band Element of Crime. Written in German, it follows Frank Lehmann, a bartender in West Berlin's Kreuzberg district, through the months before the Berlin Wall falls in 1989.

title: High Fidelity
author: Nick Hornby
blurb: High Fidelity is Nick Hornby's 1995 novel about Rob Fleming, the owner of a failing record shop in north London. After his girlfriend leaves, Rob revisits his past relationships and ranks them in the same way he compiles his lists of favorite albums.

title: How to Be Good
author: Nick Hornby
blurb: How to Be Good is a 2001 novel by Nick Hornby, narrated by Katie Carr, a doctor in North London. Her marriage is strained when her sarcastic husband undergoes a sudden change of character, which prompts her to question her own ideas of what it means to be a good person.

title: Jesus' Son
author: Denis Johnson
blurb: Jesus' Son is a 1992 collection of linked short stories by Denis Johnson. A drifting narrator named Fuckhead recounts episodes of addiction, petty crime, and chance encounters in the American Midwest and Southwest.

title: Jim the Boy
author: Tony Earley
blurb: Jim the Boy is a 2000 novel by Tony Earley, set in rural North Carolina in the 1930s. It follows Jim Glass, a boy of 10 raised by his widowed mother and three uncles, through a year of small-town childhood.

title: Kay's Lucky Coin Variety
author: Ann Y. K. Choi
blurb: Kay's Lucky Coin Variety is a novel by the Toronto-based writer Ann Y. K. Choi. It follows a Korean-Canadian family connected to a small corner store, and covers themes of immigration, family, and daily life in Toronto.

title: Kicking the Sky
author: Anthony de Sa
blurb: Kicking the Sky is a 2013 novel by Canadian author Anthony De Sa. Set in Toronto's Portuguese community in 1977, it follows a boy named Antonio whose neighborhood is shaken by the murder of a young shoeshine worker.

title: Mao II
author: Don DeLillo
blurb: Mao II is a 1991 novel by Don DeLillo about Bill Gray, a reclusive American novelist who has withdrawn from public life. His decision to be photographed draws him toward a hostage crisis in Beirut, and the book explores crowds, terrorism, and the place of the writer in modern culture.

title: Neue Vahr Süd
author: Sven Regener
blurb: Neue Vahr Süd is a 2004 German novel by Sven Regener, set in Bremen in 1981. Its protagonist, Frank Lehmann, turns 20, serves in the army, and moves in a shared flat, in a story that forms part of the series about the character that also includes Herr Lehmann.

title: Selected Poems
author: E. E. Cummings
blurb: Selected Poems collects work by the American poet E. E. Cummings. It includes his experimental typography, unusual punctuation, and lowercase style, along with love poems, satirical verse, and portraits of city life.

title: Shampoo Planet
author: Douglas Coupland
blurb: Shampoo Planet is a 1992 novel by the Canadian writer Douglas Coupland. Its narrator, Tyler Johnson, is a young man in Lancaster, California, who cares about style and travels to Europe, and the story follows his relationships with his bohemian mother and his friends.

title: Surfacing
author: Margaret Atwood
blurb: Surfacing is a 1972 novel by the Canadian writer Margaret Atwood. An unnamed narrator travels with her boyfriend and two friends to a remote island in northern Quebec to search for her missing father, and the trip leads her to confront her past.

title: Sämtliche Werke
author: Nikolai Gogol
blurb: Sämtliche Werke is a German-language edition of the collected works of Nikolai Gogol. The Russian writer's satirical novel Dead Souls, his St. Petersburg tales, and his plays such as The Government Inspector are the central texts in a collection of this kind.

title: The Bedroom Secrets of the Master Chefs
author: Irvine Welsh
blurb: The Bedroom Secrets of the Master Chefs is a 2006 novel by the Scottish author Irvine Welsh. Set in Edinburgh and told largely in dialect, it follows a food inspector, a bitter chef, and a young woman whose lives intersect around an inheritance, with Welsh's usual dark comedy.

title: The Business
author: Iain Banks
blurb: The Business is a 1999 novel by Iain Banks about Kellie Peters, a senior executive at the Caledonian Highland Company, a secretive family-run global enterprise. When the firm considers seeking a seat in the United Nations, she is drawn into its plans and her own personal choices.

title: The Crow Road
author: Iain Banks
blurb: The Crow Road is a 1992 novel by Iain Banks. Prentice McHoan returns to his family's Scottish home and tries to learn what happened to his uncle Rory, who vanished years earlier, while the McHoan and Urvill families go through births, deaths, and weddings.

title: The Innocent
author: Ian McEwan
blurb: The Innocent is a 1990 novel by Ian McEwan, set in Berlin during the early Cold War. A young British technician, Leonard Marnham, is assigned to a joint Anglo-American project to tap Soviet communications, and he becomes entangled in a relationship that ends in violence.

title: The Kite Runner
author: Khaled Hosseini
blurb: The Kite Runner is a 2003 debut novel by Khaled Hosseini. It follows Amir, a boy from Kabul, his friendship with Hassan, the son of his father's servant, and the guilt that draws him back to Afghanistan years later after emigrating to the United States.

title: The Lovely Bones
author: Alice Sebold
blurb: The Lovely Bones is a 2002 novel by Alice Sebold. Susie Salmon, a girl murdered at age fourteen, narrates from her own heaven as she watches her family and her killer in a Pennsylvania suburb in the 1970s.

title: The Master and Margarita
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
blurb: The Master and Margarita is a novel by the Russian writer Mikhail Bulgakov, written in the 1930s and first published in the 1960s. The devil arrives in Soviet Moscow with a retinue that disrupts the literary establishment, while a parallel narrative retells the story of Pontius Pilate.

title: The Mysterious Flame of Queen Loana
author: Umberto Eco
blurb: The Mysterious Flame of Queen Loana is a 2004 illustrated novel by Umberto Eco. A Milan antiquarian bookseller who has lost his autobiographical memory after a stroke returns to his family home in the countryside and searches through old books, comics, records, and papers to recover his past.

title: The Pickwick Papers
author: Charles Dickens
blurb: The Pickwick Papers is Charles Dickens's first novel, published in serial form in 1836 and 1837. Samuel Pickwick and the members of his club travel through the English countryside and meet a run of comic characters, including the servant Sam Weller.

title: The Secret Agent
author: Joseph Conrad
blurb: The Secret Agent is a 1907 novel by Joseph Conrad, set in London in the 1880s. It follows Adolf Verloc, a shopkeeper who also works as a spy and provocateur, whose assignment to provoke an anarchist outrage leads to a bombing at the Greenwich Observatory.

title: The Shipping News
author: E. Annie Proulx
blurb: The Shipping News is a 1993 novel by E. Annie Proulx, set largely in Newfoundland. Quoyle, a struggling newspaper reporter from New York, moves with his daughters to his ancestral home on the island and takes a job covering the shipping news for a local paper.

title: The Short Stories of Ernest Hemingway
author: Ernest Hemingway
blurb: The Short Stories of Ernest Hemingway collects the American author's short fiction. It includes the Nick Adams stories, tales of war, hunting, and bullfighting, and well known pieces such as The Snows of Kilimanjaro and Hills Like White Elephants.

title: The Time Traveler's Wife
author: Audrey Niffenegger
blurb: The Time Traveler's Wife is a 2003 debut novel by Audrey Niffenegger. It tells the story of Henry DeTamble, who has a genetic disorder that moves him unpredictably through time, and Clare Abshire, who meets him at different ages throughout her life in Chicago.

title: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle
author: Haruki Murakami
blurb: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle is a 1994 to 1995 novel by Haruki Murakami, set in Tokyo. An unemployed man searches for his missing cat and then his missing wife, and meets a cast of unusual characters while the story moves between modern Japan and wartime Manchuria.

title: Through Black Spruce
author: Joseph Boyden
blurb: Through Black Spruce is a 2008 novel by Canadian author Joseph Boyden. Will Bird, a Cree trapper in northern Ontario, lies in a coma while his niece Annie travels to Toronto, Montreal, and New York to search for her missing sister Suzanne.

title: White Teeth
author: Zadie Smith
blurb: White Teeth is Zadie Smith's 2000 debut novel, set in north London. It follows the families of Archie Jones, an Englishman, and Samad Iqbal, a Bangladeshi immigrant, across several decades, covering friendship, immigration, religion, and the conflicts between generations.

title: Bad Monkey
author: Carl Hiaasen
blurb: Bad Monkey is a 2013 comic crime novel by Carl Hiaasen, set in the Florida Keys and the Bahamas. A demoted police detective turned restaurant inspector investigates a severed arm found by a fishing tourist, and the case leads to a trail of corrupt developers and voodoo.

title: Berlin Game
author: Len Deighton
blurb: Berlin Game is the 1983 novel that begins Len Deighton's Bernard Samson series. London intelligence officer Samson goes to East Berlin to extract a valuable agent, and the mission opens a hunt for a mole inside his own department.

title: Bleeding Hearts
author: Ian Rankin
blurb: Bleeding Hearts is a 1994 thriller by the Scottish writer Ian Rankin, published under the pseudonym Jack Harvey. Its plot follows Michael Doyle, an assassin hired for a job in the United States, whose assignment is complicated by an FBI agent and a woman from his past.

title: Casino Royale
author: Ian Fleming
blurb: Casino Royale is the first James Bond novel by Ian Fleming, published in 1953. British agent Bond is sent to a French casino to bankrupt Le Chiffre, a paymaster for a Soviet-linked union, in a high-stakes game of baccarat.

title: Clown Town
author: Mick Herron
blurb: Clown Town is a Slough House novel by Mick Herron. The series follows a group of exiled British intelligence officers who have been reassigned to a decaying London office, under their irascible boss Jackson Lamb.

title: Country of the Blind
author: Christopher Brookmyre
blurb: Country of the Blind is the 1997 debut novel by the Scottish writer Christopher Brookmyre. Set in Scotland, it combines a political murder, a dark comic plot, and a reporter investigating the death of a Tory MP at a country house gathering.

title: Das Russlandhaus
author: John le Carré
blurb: Das Russlandhaus is the German edition of The Russia House, a 1989 Cold War spy novel by John le Carré. Barley Blair, a British publisher in Moscow, becomes the link for a Soviet scientist's manuscript on military secrets, and British and American intelligence services take an interest.

title: Death and the Oxford Box
author: Veronica Stallwood
blurb: Death and the Oxford Box is a mystery by Veronica Stallwood in her series about the crime novelist Kate Ivory. Set in Oxford, it follows Kate as she gets drawn into an investigation of a death with links to the city's academic world.

title: Der Sommermörder
author: Nicci French
blurb: Der Sommermörder is the German edition of Beneath the Skin, the 1997 psychological thriller by Nicci French, the joint pen name of Nicci Gerrard and Sean French. Three women in London receive threatening letters from a man who then begins to attack them.

title: Faceless Killers
author: Henning Mankell
blurb: Faceless Killers is the first Kurt Wallander novel by the Swedish author Henning Mankell, published in 1991. Inspector Wallander investigates the brutal murder of an elderly farming couple in southern Sweden, and the case stirs up local tension about immigration.

title: Final Orbit
author: Chris Hadfield
blurb: Final Orbit is the third Cold War space thriller by Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield, after The Apollo Murders and The Defector. Set around the 1975 Apollo-Soyuz mission, it brings back NASA flight controller Kaz Zemeckis as a deadly accident threatens US and Soviet cooperation.

title: Firewall
author: Henning Mankell
blurb: Firewall is a 1998 novel by the Swedish author Henning Mankell and the eighth Kurt Wallander mystery. When a man dies of a heart attack at a cash machine in Ystad, Wallander investigates and finds a link to a plot against the country's financial systems.

title: From Russia with Love
author: Ian Fleming
blurb: From Russia with Love is the fifth James Bond novel by Ian Fleming, published in 1957. Soviet counterintelligence plans to discredit and kill Bond through a trap involving a Soviet cipher clerk, and the plot leads him to Istanbul and the Orient Express.

title: House of Correction
author: Nicci French
blurb: House of Correction is a 2021 standalone thriller by Nicci French, the pen name of the couple Nicci Gerrard and Sean French. Tabitha Hardy, a woman charged with murder and held in prison, works to prove she has been framed.

title: Inferno
author: Dan Brown
blurb: Inferno is a 2013 thriller by Dan Brown and the fourth novel featuring Harvard symbologist Robert Langdon. Langdon wakes in a Florence hospital with memory loss and follows clues drawn from Dante's Divine Comedy while pursued by agents tied to a genetic engineer.

title: LaBrava
author: Elmore Leonard
blurb: LaBrava is a 1983 crime novel by Elmore Leonard, set in Miami Beach. Joe LaBrava, a former Secret Service agent working as a photographer, meets a faded film actress and becomes entangled in a blackmail and kidnapping plot.

title: Lucky You
author: Carl Hiaasen
blurb: Lucky You is a 2000 novel by Carl Hiaasen. Two Florida residents share a winning lottery ticket worth millions, and a pair of white supremacists plan to take the money, which leads to a chase across the state's backroads.

title: Never End
author: Åke Edwardson
blurb: Never End is a Gothenburg-set crime novel by the Swedish author Åke Edwardson, first published in Swedish in 2000 and translated into English by Laurie Thompson. Chief Inspector Erik Winter investigates the murder of a young woman in a park, which echoes an unsolved case from years earlier.

title: One Fine Day in the Middle of the Night
author: Christopher Brookmyre
blurb: One Fine Day in the Middle of the Night is a 1999 comic thriller by the Scottish writer Christopher Brookmyre. A school reunion held on a converted North Sea oil rig turns into a hostage crisis when armed mercenaries arrive, and a few former classmates try to rescue the others.

title: Quite Ugly One Morning
author: Christopher Brookmyre
blurb: Quite Ugly One Morning is the 1996 debut novel by Scottish author Christopher Brookmyre and the first to feature journalist Jack Parlabane. Parlabane investigates a murder in Edinburgh that leads him toward a conspiracy inside the National Health Service.

title: Reamde
author: Neal Stephenson
blurb: Reamde is a 2011 thriller by Neal Stephenson. A ransomware attack on a popular online fantasy game draws in a game company founder, his niece, and a group of criminals and jihadists, and the plot travels from North America to China and beyond.

title: Restless
author: William Boyd
blurb: Restless is a 2006 spy novel by William Boyd. A young woman in 1970s England learns that her mother was a British agent during the Second World War, and she reads her mother's account of her recruitment and work.

title: Road Dogs
author: Elmore Leonard
blurb: Road Dogs is a 2009 novel by Elmore Leonard. Bank robber Jack Foley, newly out of prison, and his former cellmate Cundo Rey, a Cuban con man, settle in Los Angeles, where Foley meets a woman who works as a psychic.

title: Skinny Dip
author: Carl Hiaasen
blurb: Skinny Dip is a 2004 comic crime novel by Carl Hiaasen, set in Florida. After a man throws his wife off a cruise ship, she survives, and she conspires with an eccentric former police officer to unsettle him while he is involved in a scheme polluting the Everglades.

title: Slow Horses
author: Mick Herron
blurb: Slow Horses is the first novel in Mick Herron's Slough House series, published in 2010. It follows a group of disgraced MI5 officers exiled to a run-down office, who become involved in the kidnapping of a young British Pakistani man.

title: Strandkorbkrimis
blurb: Strandkorbkrimis is a German-language anthology of short crime stories set on the Baltic coast, where the hooded beach chair, or Strandkorb, is a familiar sight.

title: Tears of the Giraffe
author: Alexander McCall Smith
blurb: Tears of the Giraffe is the second novel in Alexander McCall Smith's No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency series, set in Botswana. Precious Ramotswe takes on a case concerning an American mother whose son vanished a decade earlier, while her domestic life changes at home in Gaborone.

title: The Blood of Angels
author: Michael Marshall
blurb: The Blood of Angels is a 2005 thriller by Michael Marshall, the third book to feature Ward Hopkins and the group known as the Straw Men. Ward is drawn back into a search for answers about a serial killer network and his own past.

title: The Department of Rare Books and Special Collections
author: Eva Jurczyk
blurb: The Department of Rare Books and Special Collections is a 2022 novel by Canadian author Eva Jurczyk. Set at a university library, it follows a librarian who investigates after a valuable manuscript goes missing during a change in the department's leadership.

title: The Devil's Feather
author: Minette Walters
blurb: The Devil's Feather is a 2005 crime novel by the British writer Minette Walters. Journalist Connie Burns, investigating a series of murders linked to a mercenary in Sierra Leone, finds he has followed her to England, and the story moves between West Africa and a quiet English village.

title: The Ethical Assassin
author: David Liss
blurb: The Ethical Assassin is a 2006 comic thriller by David Liss, set in Florida in 1980. A teenage encyclopedia salesman knocks on the wrong door and meets a hit man who follows a personal code of ethics, which draws him into a chain of killings.

title: The Full Cupboard of Life
author: Alexander McCall Smith
blurb: The Full Cupboard of Life is the fifth novel in Alexander McCall Smith's No. 1 Ladies' Detective Agency series. Precious Ramotswe, Botswana's first female private detective, takes on a client who needs to choose among four suitors.

title: The Get
author: Dietrich Kalteis
blurb: The Get is a crime novel by the Canadian author Dietrich Kalteis, published by ECW Press.

title: The Girl Who Played with Fire
author: Stieg Larsson
blurb: The Girl Who Played with Fire is the second novel in Stieg Larsson's Millennium series, published in 2006. Lisbeth Salander becomes the prime suspect in a triple murder, and the journalist Mikael Blomkvist investigates to clear her name.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo
author: Stieg Larsson
blurb: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is the first novel in Stieg Larsson's Millennium series, published in Swedish in 2005. Journalist Mikael Blomkvist and hacker Lisbeth Salander work together to find out what happened to a member of a wealthy industrial family who disappeared decades earlier.

title: The Impossible Fortune
author: Richard Osman
blurb: The Impossible Fortune is the fifth novel in Richard Osman's Thursday Murder Club series. The retirees of Coopers Chase, a village for older residents in Kent, take on another case as Elizabeth, Joyce, Ibrahim, and Ron examine a link to a missing fortune.

title: The Return of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
blurb: The Return of Sherlock Holmes is a 1905 collection of 13 short stories by Arthur Conan Doyle. It brings the detective back after his apparent death at Reichenbach Falls, and includes cases such as The Adventure of the Dancing Men and The Adventure of the Six Napoleons.

title: The Sacred Art of Stealing
author: Christopher Brookmyre
blurb: The Sacred Art of Stealing is a 2002 novel by Christopher Brookmyre. Angelique de Xavia, a bank robber who leaves no trace, plans her heists in Glasgow while detective Zoe Cameron and a former thief trail her.

title: The Snowman
author: Jo Nesbø
blurb: The Snowman is a 2007 crime novel by the Norwegian author Jo Nesbø, the seventh book to feature Oslo detective Harry Hole. Hole investigates a series of disappearances of married women that coincide with the first snowfall, and he suspects a killer who leaves snowmen at the scenes.

title: Three Bags Full
author: Leonie Swann
blurb: Three Bags Full is a 2005 mystery by the German author Leonie Swann, subtitled A Sheep Detective Story. A flock of sheep in Ireland sets out to find out who killed their shepherd, using their own observations and limited knowledge of human behavior.

title: Tokyo Express
author: Seichō Matsumoto
blurb: Tokyo Express is a 1958 mystery by Japanese author Seichō Matsumoto. Two detectives take apart an apparent double suicide, and the case turns on a precisely timed railway journey and a seemingly perfect alibi.

title: All Tomorrow's Parties
author: William Gibson
blurb: All Tomorrow's Parties is a 1999 science fiction novel by William Gibson and the third book in his Bridge trilogy. Set in a near-future San Francisco, it follows characters including Colin Laney, who sees patterns in data, as events converge on a coming cultural shift.

title: Consider Phlebas
author: Iain M. Banks
blurb: Consider Phlebas is the first Culture novel by Iain M. Banks, published in 1987. Horza, a shapeshifting mercenary who sides with the Idirans, is sent on a mission during the war between the Idirans and the Culture, a post-scarcity civilization run by artificial minds.

title: Douglas Adams's Starship Titanic
author: Terry Jones
blurb: Douglas Adams's Starship Titanic is a 1997 novel by Terry Jones, adapted from the computer game that Douglas Adams created. A luxury spaceship leaves for its maiden voyage and malfunctions, and the humans who board it meet a crew of eccentric robots.

title: Feersum Endjinn
author: Iain M. Banks
blurb: Feersum Endjinn is a 1994 science fiction novel by Iain M. Banks that stands apart from his Culture series. It is set in a far-future castle on a dying Earth, and one of its narrators is written in phonetic spelling.

title: Hyperion
author: Dan Simmons
blurb: Hyperion is a 1989 science fiction novel by Dan Simmons, the first of the Hyperion Cantos. Seven pilgrims travel to the Time Tombs on a distant world, where the Shrike waits, and each tells a story of how they came to make the journey.

title: Pattern Recognition
author: William Gibson
blurb: Pattern Recognition is a 2003 novel by William Gibson. Cayce Pollard, a marketing consultant with a sensitivity to corporate logos, travels from New York to London, Tokyo, and Moscow to find the maker of a series of mysterious online film fragments.

title: Pollen
author: Jeff Noon
blurb: Pollen is a 1995 science fiction novel by the British author Jeff Noon, set in the Manchester of the Vurt universe. A detective investigates a death linked to a plague of pollen, and the novel combines drugs, feathers, and dream-like technology in a surreal near future.

title: Snow Crash
author: Neal Stephenson
blurb: Snow Crash is a 1992 science fiction novel by Neal Stephenson. Hiro Protagonist, a pizza deliverer and hacker in a near-future America of franchise territories, investigates a computer virus in the virtual Metaverse that also affects people in the physical world.

title: The Algebraist
author: Iain M. Banks
blurb: The Algebraist is a 2004 standalone science fiction novel by Iain M. Banks. Fassin Taak, a scholar, studies the Dwellers who inhabit gas giants, and his research draws him into a war between rival powers over a buried secret.

title: The Hydrogen Sonata
author: Iain M. Banks
blurb: The Hydrogen Sonata is a 2012 novel by Iain M. Banks and the tenth Culture novel. It is set around the Gzilt civilization, whose members prepare to Sublime, and a plot about a secret in the Gzilt's past draws in the Culture's warships and minds.

title: Use of Weapons
author: Iain M. Banks
blurb: Use of Weapons is a 1990 Culture novel by Iain M. Banks. Its chapters alternate between the current mission of Cheradenine Zakalwe, a mercenary employed by the Culture, and episodes from his earlier life that run in reverse order.

title: Virtual Light
author: William Gibson
blurb: Virtual Light is a 1993 novel by William Gibson and the first book of his Bridge trilogy. In a near future California, a bicycle courier named Chevette Washington steals a pair of sunglasses that hold valuable data, and she is soon pursued.

title: A Dirty Job
author: Christopher Moore
blurb: A Dirty Job is a 2006 comic fantasy by Christopher Moore, set in San Francisco. Charlie Asher, a beta male who runs a secondhand shop, becomes a Death Merchant who collects the souls of the dying, which leaves him managing his infant daughter alongside his new duties.

title: Fool
author: Christopher Moore
blurb: Fool is a 2009 comic retelling of Shakespeare's King Lear by Christopher Moore. The story follows Pocket, the king's jester, who narrates events in a bawdy voice as Lear's daughters scheme for power in a fictional Britain.

title: Good Omens
author: Terry Pratchett; Neil Gaiman
blurb: Good Omens is a 1990 comic novel written by Terry Pratchett and Neil Gaiman. An angel and a demon who have grown comfortable on Earth try to head off the end of the world after the Antichrist is misplaced as a baby.

title: Heroes
author: Stephen Fry
blurb: Heroes is a 2018 retelling of Greek myths by Stephen Fry, the second volume after Mythos. It covers the tales of Perseus, Heracles, Jason, Atalanta, Theseus, and other mortal figures, written in an informal narrative voice with commentary on the sources.

title: Mexican Gothic
author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
blurb: Mexican Gothic is a 2020 horror novel by Silvia Moreno-Garcia, set in 1950s Mexico. Noemí Taboada, a young socialite, travels to a remote mountain mansion to check on her newly married cousin, and finds a decaying house and a secretive English family.

title: Necrophenia
author: Robert Rankin
blurb: Necrophenia is a comic novel by Robert Rankin, set in the absurd version of Brentford, the west London suburb, that runs through many of his books.

title: Schattenschwester
author: Lucinda Riley
blurb: Schattenschwester is the German edition of The Shadow Sister, the third novel in Lucinda Riley's Seven Sisters series. Star D'Aplièse, one of six adopted sisters, follows clues about her origins to London and a story from the early twentieth century.

title: Tailchaser's Song
author: Tad Williams
blurb: Tailchaser's Song is the 1985 debut novel by Tad Williams. Fritti Tailchaser, a young tomcat, leaves his home to search for a missing friend, and his travels bring him into the secret world of cat society, myths, and dangers.

title: The City of Brass
author: S. A. Chakraborty
blurb: The City of Brass is the 2017 debut novel by S. A. Chakraborty and the first in the Daevabad trilogy. Nahri, a con artist in eighteenth century Cairo, learns she has magical powers and is taken to the hidden djinn city of Daevabad.

title: The Lord of the Rings
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
blurb: The Lord of the Rings is J. R. R. Tolkien's high fantasy epic, published in three volumes in 1954 and 1955. Frodo Baggins and a fellowship set out to destroy the One Ring in Mordor, in a conflict that shapes the future of Middle-earth.

title: The Return of the King
author: J. R. R. Tolkien
blurb: The Return of the King is the third volume of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings, published in 1955. The war against Sauron reaches its climax at Minas Tirith and the Black Gate, while Frodo and Sam make their way into Mordor to destroy the Ring.

title: The Truth
author: Terry Pratchett
blurb: The Truth is the twenty-fifth Discworld novel by Terry Pratchett, published in 2000. William de Worde starts the Discworld's first newspaper in Ankh-Morpork, and his reporting draws him into a plot against the city's ruler, Lord Vetinari.

title: Unseen Academicals
author: Terry Pratchett
blurb: Unseen Academicals is a 2009 Discworld novel by Terry Pratchett. It follows the wizards of Unseen University as they revive the old street game of football in Ankh-Morpork, while Mr. Nutt, a candle dribbler, and a cook named Juliet become involved.

title: Whitechapel Gods
author: S. M. Peters
blurb: Whitechapel Gods is a 2008 steampunk novel by S. M. Peters, set in a walled-off district of Victorian London ruled by two machine gods. A resistance group of outcasts inside the district tries to overthrow them.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
author: Anthony Doerr
blurb: All the Light We Cannot See is a 2014 novel by Anthony Doerr. It alternates between Marie-Laure, a blind French girl, and Werner, a German orphan with a talent for radios, whose paths approach each other in occupied Saint-Malo during World War Two.

title: Baudolino
author: Umberto Eco
blurb: Baudolino is a 2000 historical novel by the Italian writer Umberto Eco, set in the twelfth century. The title character, a peasant who becomes an adopted son of Emperor Frederick Barbarossa, tells his life story to a Byzantine historian, with travels to the mythical kingdom of Prester John.

title: Birdsong
author: Sebastian Faulks
blurb: Birdsong is a 1993 novel by Sebastian Faulks that moves between 1910 and the 1970s. It follows Stephen Wraysford, an English officer on the Western Front in the First World War, and a later descendant who researches his story.

title: Canoe Lake
author: Roy MacGregor
blurb: Canoe Lake is a 2002 novel by Roy MacGregor, a Canadian journalist and author. It takes the 1917 death of painter Tom Thomson on Ontario's Canoe Lake as its starting point and sets the story in Algonquin Park.

title: Conspiracy
author: S. J. Parris
blurb: Conspiracy is a 2013 historical mystery by S. J. Parris and the third novel featuring Giordano Bruno. Set in Elizabethan England in 1585, the former friar works as a spy for Francis Walsingham and investigates a plot to place Mary, Queen of Scots on the throne.

title: Die Säulen der Erde
author: Ken Follett
blurb: Die Säulen der Erde is the German edition of Ken Follett's The Pillars of the Earth, a 1989 historical novel. It follows the building of a cathedral in the fictional English town of Kingsbridge during the 12th century, and the civil war known as the Anarchy.

title: Dodger
author: Terry Pratchett
blurb: Dodger is a 2012 novel by Terry Pratchett, set in Victorian London. Dodger, a young tosher who scavenges in the sewers, rescues a girl from attackers and meets Charles Dickens and Henry Mayhew among the city's characters.

title: Fall of Giants
author: Ken Follett
blurb: Fall of Giants is a 2010 historical novel by Ken Follett and the first volume of the Century Trilogy. It follows five interconnected families in the United States, Britain, Germany, Russia, and Wales through the First World War and the Russian Revolution.

title: Half-Blood Blues
author: Esi Edugyan
blurb: Half-Blood Blues is a 2011 novel by the Canadian author Esi Edugyan. It follows a group of jazz musicians in Berlin and Paris in 1939 and 1940, including a young Black German trumpeter who vanishes, and their later lives in the 1990s.

title: Heartstone
author: C. J. Sansom
blurb: Heartstone is the fifth novel in C. J. Sansom's Shardlake series, set in 1545. Matthew Shardlake, a hunchbacked lawyer in the court of Henry VIII, travels to Portsmouth while France threatens invasion, and takes on a wardship case there.

title: Montenegro
author: Starling Lawrence
blurb: Montenegro is a 1997 novel by Starling Lawrence, an American editor and writer. Its story is set in the Balkans in the years before the First World War.

title: My Name Is Red
author: Orhan Pamuk
blurb: My Name Is Red is a 1998 novel by the Turkish writer Orhan Pamuk, set in Istanbul in 1591. A murder among the Ottoman court miniaturists drives the plot, and the chapters are told by multiple narrators, including the dead man, a corpse, and a coin.

title: Persona Non Grata
author: Ruth Downie
blurb: Persona Non Grata is the third novel in Ruth Downie's series about Gaius Petreius Ruso, a Roman army doctor. Ruso and his British partner Tilla travel to Gaul, where his family's debts and the death of a creditor force him to investigate.

title: The Radetzky March
author: Joseph Roth
blurb: The Radetzky March is a 1932 novel by the Austrian author Joseph Roth. It follows three generations of the Trotta family, whose fortunes are tied to the Habsburg monarchy, from the battle of Solferino to the empire's collapse after the First World War.

title: The Samurai Detectives, Vol. 1
author: Shotaro Ikenami
blurb: The Samurai Detectives is a collection of crime stories by the Japanese novelist Shōtarō Ikenami, set in Edo-period Japan and translated by Yui Kajita. It is the first volume in English of a series Ikenami wrote from 1972 to 1989.

title: When Christ and His Saints Slept
author: Sharon Kay Penman
blurb: When Christ and His Saints Slept is a 1993 historical novel by Sharon Kay Penman and the first of her Plantagenet trilogy. It covers the twelfth century civil war in England between Empress Maude and her cousin King Stephen, a period known as the Anarchy.

title: Can Holding In a Fart Kill You?
author: Andrew Thompson
blurb: Can Holding In a Fart Kill You? is a humor and science book by Andrew Thompson that answers odd questions about the body and daily life. Its short entries cover topics from digestion to household curiosities and use a conversational explanatory approach.

title: Die allerneueste klassische Sau
author: Hermann Kinder (ed.)
blurb: Die allerneueste klassische Sau is a German-language humor anthology, edited by Hermann Kinder, that collects erotic passages from classic literature. It belongs to a series that gathers suggestive and bawdy scenes from well-known writers.

title: How to Be a Canadian
author: Will Ferguson; Ian Ferguson
blurb: How to Be a Canadian is a 2001 humor book by brothers Will Ferguson and Ian Ferguson. It describes Canadian habits, history, and regional quirks in a series of comic essays for readers inside and outside the country.

title: Loriots heile Welt
author: Loriot
blurb: Loriots heile Welt is a German-language collection of cartoons and sketches by Loriot, the stage name of the German humorist Vicco von Bülow. It gathers his drawings and comic scenes depicting bourgeois life, awkward conversations, and the small mishaps of German everyday life.

title: Sh*t My Dad Says
author: Justin Halpern
blurb: Sh*t My Dad Says is a 2010 humor book by Justin Halpern, based on his popular Twitter account. It collects blunt and profane remarks by his father, Sam Halpern, a retired nephrologist in San Diego, with commentary from the author.

title: Wortkirmes
author: Robert Gernhardt
blurb: Wortkirmes is a German-language book of humorous verse and wordplay by Robert Gernhardt, a poet, cartoonist, and satirist. It collects poems and short comic pieces that play on language, rhyme, and everyday absurdity.

title: My Neighbor Totoro, Vol. 1
author: Hayao Miyazaki
blurb: My Neighbor Totoro, Vol. 1 is the first volume of the manga adaptation of the 1988 animated film by Hayao Miyazaki. Two sisters, Satsuki and Mei, move to the countryside in postwar Japan while their mother recovers in hospital, and they meet forest spirits including Totoro.

title: The Bones of Ruin
author: Sarah Raughley
blurb: The Bones of Ruin is a 2018 young adult fantasy novel by the Canadian author Sarah Raughley. Iyanu, a young woman who cannot die, is taken into a Victorian-era circus act and then to a mysterious society that explains her past.

title: The Graveyard Book
author: Neil Gaiman
blurb: The Graveyard Book is a 2008 children's novel by Neil Gaiman. A toddler escapes the murder of his family and is raised by the ghosts of a graveyard, where he learns their skills while a killer is still looking for him.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
blurb: The Little Prince is a novella by the French writer and aviator Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, first published in 1943. A pilot stranded in the Sahara meets a young prince from a small asteroid, who recounts his travels to other planets and his love for a rose.

title: The Prairie Dog Conspiracy
author: Eric Wilson
blurb: The Prairie Dog Conspiracy is a mystery for young readers by the Canadian author Eric Wilson, part of his series about the young detectives Tom and Liz Austen.

title: The Sea of Monsters
author: Rick Riordan
blurb: The Sea of Monsters is the second novel in Rick Riordan's Percy Jackson and the Olympians series, published in 2006. Percy and his friends sail into the Sea of Monsters to find the Golden Fleece and save Camp Half-Blood.

title: Cod: A Biography of the Fish That Changed the World
author: Mark Kurlansky
blurb: Cod: A Biography of the Fish That Changed the World is a 1997 book by Mark Kurlansky. It traces the history of the North Atlantic cod fishery and its role in European and American economies, from Viking voyages to modern collapse, and includes recipes from different periods.

title: Das Profil der Mörder
author: Paul Britton
blurb: Das Profil der Mörder is the German edition of The Jigsaw Man by Paul Britton, a British forensic psychologist. He describes his work in offender profiling and the investigation of serial killings and other violent crimes in Britain.

title: In Cold Blood
author: Truman Capote
blurb: In Cold Blood is Truman Capote's 1966 account of the 1959 murder of the Clutter family in Holcomb, Kansas. Capote follows the investigation and the two killers, Perry Smith and Dick Hickock, through their capture, trial, and execution, using the techniques of a novel.

title: London: The Biography
author: Peter Ackroyd
blurb: London: The Biography is a 2000 history by Peter Ackroyd. Organized by theme and without a strict chronology, it follows the city from its prehistoric origins to the present, covering its streets, trades, crime, plague, fire, and the habits of its inhabitants.

title: Londoners
author: Craig Taylor
blurb: Londoners is a 2011 oral history by Craig Taylor, built from interviews with people who live and work in London. The speakers include a cab driver, a banker, an immigrant, and a street cleaner, and they describe the city and how it changes.

title: Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil
author: John Berendt
blurb: Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil is a 1994 nonfiction book by John Berendt. It records the author's years in Savannah, Georgia, and the murder trials of the antiques dealer Jim Williams, alongside the city's colorful residents.

title: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome
author: Mary Beard
blurb: SPQR: A History of Ancient Rome is a 2015 book by the classicist Mary Beard. It covers roughly a thousand years, from the early city to the citizenship edict of 212 CE, and examines how Rome grew from a small settlement into an empire.

title: The Farfarers
author: Farley Mowat
blurb: The Farfarers is a 2012 history by Farley Mowat, the Canadian author, on the peoples who lived in the Arctic before the Vikings. It argues that a seafaring culture from northern Europe settled in the Canadian North, a claim many scholars dispute.

title: The Just
author: Jan Brokken
blurb: The Just is a work of narrative nonfiction by Dutch writer Jan Brokken. It tells the stories of diplomats and others who helped Jewish refugees escape Europe during World War Two, including Jan Zwartendijk in Lithuania and Chiune Sugihara.

title: Wayward Lives, Beautiful Experiments: Intimate Histories of Social Upheaval
author: Saidiya Hartman
blurb: Wayward Lives, Beautiful Experiments is a 2019 history by the scholar Saidiya Hartman. Drawing on archives, it recounts the lives of young Black women in early twentieth-century Philadelphia and New York, and it describes their search for freedom and intimacy in urban life.

title: Yesterday's Toronto
author: Linda Shapiro (ed.)
blurb: Yesterday's Toronto is an illustrated collection edited by Linda Shapiro, offering a look at the history of Toronto. It brings together historical photographs, drawings, and writing about the city and how it grew.

title: Sailing a Serious Ocean
author: John Kretschmer
blurb: Sailing a Serious Ocean is a sailing book by John Kretschmer, a professional offshore skipper. It draws on 30 years at sea: the boats, the storms, the crews, and the lessons learned on ocean crossings.

title: A Tour on the Prairies
author: Washington Irving
blurb: A Tour on the Prairies is a travel narrative by Washington Irving, published in 1835. Irving describes a month-long journey in 1832 through what is now Oklahoma with a party of rangers, with accounts of buffalo hunts, camp life, and encounters with the landscape.

title: A Year in Provence
author: Peter Mayle
blurb: A Year in Provence is a 1989 memoir by Peter Mayle, a British author. He describes the first year after he and his wife bought an old farmhouse in the Luberon region of southern France, covering local characters, food, builders, and the changing seasons.

title: Atlas Obscura
author: Joshua Foer; Dylan Thuras; Ella Morton
blurb: Atlas Obscura is a guidebook compiled by Joshua Foer, Dylan Thuras, and Ella Morton, drawn from the Atlas Obscura website. It catalogs hundreds of unusual, hidden, and little known places around the world, with photographs and short descriptions organized by region.

title: Dispatches from Pluto
author: Richard Grant
blurb: Dispatches from Pluto is a 2015 travel memoir by the British writer Richard Grant. After moving to the Mississippi Delta with his girlfriend, he describes the region's people, history, food, and customs, and the problems of settling in a place he finds both foreign and welcoming.

title: Germany
author: Dorling Kindersley
blurb: Germany is a travel guide published by Dorling Kindersley, a publisher known for richly illustrated guidebooks. It covers the country's regions, cities, and sights with photographs, maps, and practical information for visitors planning a trip.

title: The Complete Notes
author: Bill Bryson
blurb: The Complete Notes is an omnibus of travel writing by Bill Bryson. It brings together his humorous accounts of traveling in Britain and the United States, including Notes from a Small Island and Notes from a Big Country.

title: The Hotel Years
author: Joseph Roth
blurb: The Hotel Years is a collection of travel journalism by the Austrian writer Joseph Roth, drawn from his newspaper work between the wars. His pieces describe cities and rail journeys across Europe, written in the 1920s and 1930s while he lived in hotels, and they capture a continent in transition.

title: Travels with Charley
author: John Steinbeck
blurb: Travels with Charley is a 1962 travel narrative by John Steinbeck. He tours the United States in a customized pickup camper with his poodle, Charley, and records the people and places he meets across the country.

title: Dispatches from the Front
author: David Halton
blurb: Dispatches from the Front is David Halton's biography of his father, Matthew Halton, the CBC correspondent whose radio reports from the Second World War made him one of the best-known voices in Canada.

title: Far Out Isn't Far Enough
author: Tomi Ungerer
blurb: Far Out Isn't Far Enough is a memoir by the Alsatian-born illustrator Tomi Ungerer. It covers his childhood under Nazi occupation, his work as a children's author and satirical artist in New York, and his later life in Nova Scotia and Ireland.

title: Into the Magic Shop
author: James R. Doty
blurb: Into the Magic Shop is a 2016 memoir by James R. Doty, a neurosurgeon and Stanford professor. He describes how a magic shop and its owner helped him as a boy in a troubled household, and how the lessons later shaped his career and his work on compassion.

title: Life on Air
author: David Attenborough
blurb: Life on Air is the 2002 memoir of David Attenborough, the British broadcaster and naturalist. It traces his career at the BBC, from early television work to series such as Life on Earth, and the expeditions he made to film wildlife.

title: Me
author: Elton John
blurb: Me is the 2019 autobiography of Elton John, the British singer and songwriter. He describes his childhood in Pinner, his rise to fame in the 1970s, his songwriting partnership with Bernie Taupin, his struggles with addiction, and his later work as an advocate and father.

title: Travels with Lizbeth
author: Lars Eighner
blurb: Travels with Lizbeth is a 1993 memoir by Lars Eighner, an American writer who lived on the streets of Austin and Los Angeles for several years. He writes about life with his dog, Lizbeth, and about scavenging, shelter, and survival.

title: We Were an Island
author: Peter P. Blanchard III
blurb: We Were an Island is a biography by Peter P. Blanchard III of Art and Nan Kellam. The couple lived for decades on Placentia Island off the coast of Maine, without electricity, and later gave the island to The Nature Conservancy.

title: Clean Meat
author: Paul Shapiro
blurb: Clean Meat is a 2018 book by Paul Shapiro, an animal protection advocate. It reports on the development of meat grown from animal cells, profiling the scientists and entrepreneurs involved and discussing the technology's prospects for food production, the environment, and animal welfare.

title: Das große Katzenbuch
blurb: A German-language illustrated book about cats.

title: Entangled Life
author: Merlin Sheldrake
blurb: Entangled Life is a 2020 book by biologist Merlin Sheldrake about fungi. It explains how mycelial networks work, how fungi shape ecosystems, and how they bear on medicine, food, and the study of intelligence.

title: The World Without Us
author: Alan Weisman
blurb: The World Without Us is a 2007 book by the journalist Alan Weisman. It imagines how the planet would change if humans vanished, describing how buildings, infrastructure, and ecosystems would decay or recover, and what traces of civilization might remain for millennia.

title: You Are Here
author: Chris Hadfield
blurb: You Are Here is a 2014 book by the Canadian astronaut Chris Hadfield. It presents photographs he took of Earth from the International Space Station, with captions that describe the places and what they show.

title: Freakonomics
author: Steven D. Levitt; Stephen J. Dubner
blurb: Freakonomics is a 2005 book by economist Steven D. Levitt and journalist Stephen J. Dubner. It applies economic methods to unusual questions, such as the effects of incentives on cheaters, parents, and drug dealers.

title: Spent: Sex, Evolution, and Consumer Behavior
author: Geoffrey Miller
blurb: Spent: Sex, Evolution, and Consumer Behavior is a 2009 book by the evolutionary psychologist Geoffrey Miller. It argues that consumer choices work largely as displays of traits such as intelligence, conscientiousness, and agreeableness, and it applies evolutionary theory to marketing and shopping.

title: Stupid White Men
author: Michael Moore
blurb: Stupid White Men is a 2001 book by the American filmmaker Michael Moore, subtitled and Other Sorry Excuses for the State of the Nation. It offers a satirical and political critique of the Bush administration, corporate power, and American society.

title: The Collection
author: Peter Ackroyd
blurb: The Collection is a book by Peter Ackroyd, the English biographer and novelist. It gathers his journalism, essays, and short fiction, with a range of subjects that includes London, literature, and history.

title: The Future of Truth
author: Werner Herzog
blurb: The Future of Truth is a 2019 book by the German filmmaker Werner Herzog, translated into English. Herzog reflects on truth, fabrication, and the ways images and information shape belief, drawing on examples from his films, travels, and encounters across several decades.

title: The Way of Zen
author: Alan Watts
blurb: The Way of Zen is a 1957 book by Alan Watts that introduces Zen Buddhism to Western readers. It covers the history of the tradition from India and China to Japan, and explains its main ideas and practices.

title: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
author: Robert M. Pirsig
blurb: Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance is a 1974 book by Robert M. Pirsig. A father and his son travel across the United States by motorcycle, and the narrator uses the trip to explore questions about quality, values, and his own past.

title: Good to Great
author: Jim Collins
blurb: Good to Great is a 2001 business book by Jim Collins. His research team studied 11 companies that sustained strong stock performance after a period of average results, and the book identifies common practices such as disciplined people, disciplined thought, and disciplined action.

title: Instant: The Story of Polaroid
author: Christopher Bonanos
blurb: Instant is a 2012 history of the Polaroid Corporation by Christopher Bonanos. It follows Edwin Land, the company's founder, and traces the development of instant photography, its cultural impact, and the company's decline.

title: Principles: Life & Work
author: Ray Dalio
blurb: Principles: Life & Work is a 2017 book by Ray Dalio, founder of the investment firm Bridgewater Associates. It sets out the rules Dalio developed for decision making, relationships, and running an organization, and draws on his experience in finance.

title: Reinvention
author: Arlene Dickinson
blurb: Reinvention is a business book by Arlene Dickinson, the Canadian entrepreneur and former Dragons' Den investor. It draws on her own career setbacks and her experience advising companies, and it lays out steps for changing course in work and business.

title: Smartcuts
author: Shane Snow
blurb: Smartcuts is a 2014 business and self-improvement book by Shane Snow. It uses case studies from startups, athletes, and artists to explain how some people and organizations progress faster than expected by changing methods and systems.

title: The Entrepreneur's Playbook
author: Leonard C. Green
blurb: The Entrepreneur's Playbook is a business guide by Leonard C. Green. It lays out steps for starting and running a company, covering planning, funding, and growth, and draws on examples from the author's experience.

title: Winning
author: Jack Welch; Suzy Welch
blurb: Winning is a 2005 management book by Jack Welch, the former chairman of General Electric, written with his wife Suzy Welch. It offers advice on leadership, hiring, strategy, and career decisions, and it uses a question and answer format along with anecdotes from his time at GE.

title: 1000 Chairs
author: Charlotte Fiell; Peter Fiell
blurb: 1000 Chairs is a reference book by Charlotte and Peter Fiell, design historians. It presents a catalogue of chair designs from the 19th century to the present, with photographs and short entries on designers and manufacturers.

title: Century
author: Bruce Bernard
blurb: Century is a large format photography book edited by Bruce Bernard and published by Phaidon in 1999. It presents images from across the twentieth century, arranged chronologically, covering war, politics, art, and daily life.

title: Design of the 20th Century
author: Charlotte Fiell; Peter Fiell
blurb: Design of the 20th Century is a large illustrated survey by Charlotte and Peter Fiell, published by Taschen. It presents furniture, products, and graphics from the century's major designers and movements, organized by period with short texts and reference material.

title: The Times History of Printing
blurb: The Times History of Printing is an illustrated book on the history of printing. It is presumably a reference work that covers type, presses, and the spread of printed material.

title: 642 Things to Write About
author: San Francisco Writers' Grotto
blurb: 642 Things to Write About is a writing prompt book from the San Francisco Writers' Grotto. It contains hundreds of short exercises that cover fiction, memoir, and poetry, and it leaves space for the writer's own responses.

title: Keep Out! Build Your Own Backyard Clubhouse
author: Lee Mothes
blurb: Keep Out! Build Your Own Backyard Clubhouse is a project book by Lee Mothes. It gives plans and step-by-step directions for building small playhouses and hideouts, with materials lists, tool advice, and designs for a range of skill levels.

title: The Martha Manual
author: Martha Stewart
blurb: The Martha Manual is a 2013 household reference book by Martha Stewart. It gives practical advice on cooking, cleaning, organizing, gardening, and other everyday tasks, and is organized as a guide for running a home.
